crm_notes: Primary ask: Dedicated capacity with predictable latency for trading-chat use-case (low jitter, tail guarantees).
Customer quote: "p99 needs to be under 350ms end-to-end for non-streaming short responses; p95 can be tighter".
Concern: streaming vs non-streaming measurement. They want separate SLOs for time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and time-to-complete for non-streaming requests.

We discussed client-side timing vs server-side: customer wants E2E (client RTT + server processing + proxy time) in contract, but will accept server-only metrics for internal ops if we provide mapping methodology.
SE notes: observed non-streaming p50/p95/p99 on dedicated test pool: 90ms / 180ms / 540ms under synthetic 75th-percentile load (24h run).
Streaming behavior: median TTFB ~35ms in our lab; token streaming rate varies with batch size — important to capture as per-token latency and initial chunk latency.

Recommendation given: define SLO matrix in appendix: separate rows for small-response non-streaming (<256 tokens) and long-response streaming (>512 tokens). Use client-side E2E for billing SLA, server-side traces for operational alerts.

Agreement point: p95 non-streaming (<=256 tokens) target 200ms; p99 non-streaming target 400ms (negotiable during legal). Streaming TTFB p50 < 50ms, p95 < 120ms for first chunk; per-token steady-state <= 15ms per token at configured batch size.

Measurement alignment: capture these signals in dashboards: client_rtt, server_queue_ms, server_compute_ms, proxy_ms, ttfb_ms, tail_latency_ms. Annotate percentiles and sample rate (1% tracing + full aggregates every 1m).

Important nuance recorded: percentiles must be computed on the same population. Customer insisted we not mix streaming partial-chunk latencies into non-streaming percentiles (will create separate metrics).
SLA language points they asked to include: measurement window (30d rolling), burn rate thresholds for credits, and whether retries/fallbacks are excluded from tail calculations.
Tests to run: 72h soak with client-shaped bursts (peak ~600 RPS), regional routing to NA zone, and disabled autoscaling to validate reserved capacity behavior.
Operational ask: export a mapping doc that translates our server-side percentiles to expected client E2E given median 25ms network RTT and customer proxy adds 10-20ms.

Open technical blocker: need clarity on how batching will be represented in SLA (batched requests can change p50/p95 trade-offs). Customer expects Redwood to document batching behavior per model-profile.
Pricing ask: confirm committed GPU reservation count and burst allowances; they prefer a burst pool over minutes-to-scale autoscale for predictable tail performance.
Quote from SE: "We should include explicit instrumentation for TTFB and per-token inter-arrival; otherwise the p99 will be misleading when streaming is used."
